name: IRS.gov
notice: A layout study, not IRS.gov and not a government website: three IRS pages rebuilt with Golden Grids as GIFrs, a parody name. Not affiliated with the IRS; nothing here signs in, files or pays.
summary: Three pages of IRS.gov (the home page, Make a payment, and Online account for individuals) rebuilt as stacked golden grids. The words are the IRS's; the site around them is not.

reviewed.method: Captured at 390, 820 and 1440 pixels, with each page's main text saved alongside. The IRS's own last-reviewed dates are printed on the pages that carry them.

real: The text. It is the Internal Revenue Service's, a work of the United States government in the public domain (17 U.S.C. § 105), shortened and rearranged but not reworded in substance.
The limits, fees and dates, as those pages gave them on the day they were captured. They may have changed; check IRS.gov.
invented: The site. GIFrs is a parody name made for this study; it is not an agency, and this is not a government website.
Every control. Nothing here signs anyone in, files a return, makes a payment or downloads a form.
The icons, which were drawn for the study. No IRS seal, logo or mark is used.
owner: the Internal Revenue Service, the Department of the Treasury or any government agency
